newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds firm, Norfolk trading eyed.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds firm, Norfolk trading eyed.

text.p: Corporate bond spreads to U.S. Treasuries held firm on Thursday in light secondary trading as players once again focused on Norfolk Southern's deal - this time in the aftermarket, dealers said.
Spreads to U.S. Treasuries were unchanged across most maturities, with bank and industrial paper seen a touch tighter, they said.
"It's been a fairly quiet day...we did see some better retail activity though," one trader said. "Right now we're just waiting to see Norfolk Southern's deal free up."
Corporate bond players said the deal which was largely oversubscribed is expected to tighten a few basis points on the break.
On Wednesday, railroad firm, Norfolk Southern Corp issued a $4.3 billion multi-tranche debt offering, making it the largest investment-grade deal to hit the corporate bond market.
JP Morgan Securities who jointly underwrote the offering with co-lead manager Merrill Lynch & Co, said demand was strongest for longer maturities.
